messages:
alex: FYI saw a jump in token latency on canary with the stable 7B model. KV cache hit_rate dropped from ~0.78 -> ~0.49 between 19:10-19:25. Posting traces and queries. :eyes:

maria: ugh. which route? /chat or /generate?

alex: /generate primarily. route tag: tenant=search-service. pprof: https://rdev/pprof/abc123

jin: looking now — CPU flame shows more time in kernel-selection and a larger tail in kv lookup. Also seeing more cache misses. Might be batching heuristic change from the morning deploy.

ops-analytics: quick prom query that flagged it:
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total{env="canary"}[5m])) by (route)
```
spike for route="search-service/generate" at ~19:12.

maria: and evictions rose too. snapshot by alloc class:
```
kv_cache_evictions_total{alloc_class="small"} 120
kv_cache_evictions_total{alloc_class="large"} 7
```

alex: reproduced locally by toggling kernel A->B in config. kernel B increases cycles inside kv lookup loop (~1.6x).

jin: could the batching heuristic be producing larger batches for this tenant which increases cache churn? we bumped batch timeout yesterday.

maria: proposal: add per-route metrics: prefix_reuse_ratio, mem_footprint_by_route, and per-token latency phase breakdown. e.g. token_serve_ns{phase="kv_lookup"|"kernel_exec"|"writeback"} so we can waterfall.

alex: agreed. i'll open a dashboard PR with panels: per-route hit_rate, evictions/sec, mem_by_route, prefix_reuse_ratio, token_serve_ns waterfall, and an alert: hit_rate < 0.6 for 3m on critical routes.

jin: +1. also add route attribution tag to cache keys (model+route) so reuse_by_route is precise.

sre-bot: Deploy rule: auto-rollback canary if hit_rate < 0.6 for 5m. :robot_face:

maria: thanks — will iterate on queries in the dashboard thread after the PR lands.
